key_insight: VideoAR is a scalable visual-autoregressive framework that generates videos by combining multi-scale next-frame and scale prediction with intra-frame VAR modeling, disentangling spatial and temporal factors to deliver high-quality video with lower compute than diffusion/flow approaches.
problem_solved: Diffusion and flow-matching video generators are high-quality but computationally expensive and hard to scale to long or high-resolution videos; VideoAR addresses slow sampling, heavy compute, and entangled spatial–temporal modeling by using an autoregressive, multi-scale next-frame design.
method: Multi-scale next-frame & scale prediction: generate frames coarse-to-fine and predict scale information to refine spatial detail efficiently.
Intra-frame Visual Autoregressive (VAR) modeling: capture spatial dependencies within each frame autoregressively for sharp image quality.
Causal inter-frame autoregression: predict future frames sequentially (next-frame) to model temporal dynamics while keeping sampling and memory costs manageable.
impact: Provides practitioners a more compute-efficient, scalable alternative for high-quality video generation that enables faster sampling and easier extension to longer or higher-resolution videos and downstream tasks like conditional video synthesis.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: blocks for intra-frame VAR, multiscale prediction, and causal next-frame flow with arrows showing information flow.
Coarse-to-fine timeline: a sequence of frames showing multiscale refinement from low to high resolution.
Bar/line chart: compute cost and sampling speed vs. diffusion/flow models (e.g., FLOPs or latency vs. FID/PSNR).
Qualitative grid: rows of generated video clips next to ground truth to show visual fidelity across time and scales.
paper_title: VideoAR: Autoregressive Video Generation via Next-Frame & Scale Prediction
paper_authors: Longbin Ji, Xiaoxiong Liu, Junyuan Shang, Shuohuan Wang, Yu Sun
